## Beat 1 — Problem (0:00–0:20)

> This is Mia. She is six, and tonight she is stuck on one small sound.
>
> *Mmm.*
>
> Her teacher has a full classroom. Her nanay is still at work. And the signal at home is gone again.
>
> So Mia closes the book.

## Beat 2 — Solution (0:20–0:40)

> Then someone small, with very big eyes, peeks in.
>
> **LILY:** Hi there! I'm so happy you're here. Let's play and learn together!
>
> This is Lily, and this is PlayIT: a phonics game for Grade 1 learners. It follows DepEd's Marungko order, listens to the child, and works offline.

## Beat 3 — Demonstration (0:40–1:10)

> No Wi-Fi needed. Mia just taps her letter.
>
> First, she hears it. Then she says it,
>
> *"Mouse!"*
>
> and the phone itself checks her voice. Nothing leaves the device.
>
> Miss it? Lily never scolds. She shows the mouth shape and says it with her.
>
> Next, she finds the pictures that start with the sound. Then the letters blend into real words.
>
> And parents get a plain progress report.

## Beat 4 — Results and validation (1:10–1:40)

> We tested with **30** people: **16** children, plus **5** parents and **9** teachers.
>
> **15** of **16** children chose the happy face, and **14** of **16** would play it again.
>
> The grown-ups who open the door? Parents gave it **4.6** for Grade 1 fit, **4.4** to recommend. Teachers scored teaching **4.7**.

## Notes

- Children are the users; parents and teachers are the bridge. They decide whether the app reaches a child, which is why their ratings are in the pitch. Keep the two groups' numbers separate.
- Mia is a story character, not a survey participant. Do not present her as a real case.
- Mia's "Mouse!" in Beat 3 is your own voice, saying the Say It word shown on the real app screen.
- The numbers are frozen (12 Nov) at 30 participants across Rounds 1 and 2: the children's smiley-face answers and the parents' ratings are from Round 1; the teachers' teaching score (4.7) is the Round 2 rubric, answered by 5 of the 9 teachers. Later answers go to the research paper only.
- The teacher quote is real and comes from Round 1 (teacher T-1).
- The 691 automated tests stay on the poster only. They were cut from the pitch on 11 Nov: viewers do not need them, and the cut lets Beat 4 run at a natural pace.
- If you run long, cut "And parents get a plain progress report" from Beat 3 and show it on screen only.
